chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, who said:

I wrote to Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him) that I have three thousand dirhams due from a man, and those dirhams used to be spent (in circulation) among the people in those days, but they are not being spent today. So is the debt upon him for those very dirhams exactly, or for whatever is being spent today among the people? He (peace be upon him) wrote to me: 'For you is that you should take from him whatever is being spent among the people, just as you gave him whatever was being spent among the people.'

key_terms.الرِّضَا: Al-Rida (The Satisfied One, a title for the Imam)
key_terms.بِأَعْيَانِهَا: In their very selves/exactly (referring to the specific coins)
key_terms.تَنْفُقُ: Spent/Circulated (used here to mean in circulation as currency)

ai.seo_question: How should a debt be repaid if the currency's value has changed since the loan was taken?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) establishes the principle of 'fi al-thaman' (in the price/value) rather than 'fi al-'ayn' (in the specific object) for debt repayment, addressing the historical context of currency debasement and inflation. It clarifies that when a specific currency loses purchasing power, the debtor is obligated to repay the equivalent current market value, ensuring fairness to the creditor. This ruling is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for handling monetary debts in fluctuating economic conditions.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus who said,

‘I wrote to Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> that for me are three thousand Dirhams upon a man, and those Dirhams used to be spent between the people in those days (normal currency), and these are not being spent today (in circulation). So is there (a debt) upon him of those very Dirhams exactly or whatever is being spend (in circulation) today between the people?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> wrote to me: ‘For you is that you should take from him what is being spent (in circulation) between the people just as you had given it to him what was being spend (in circulation) between the people’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus who has said

the following: “I once wrote to al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and asked, ’A man owes to me three thousand dirham which were in circulation at that time among people, but today they are not in circulation among people; if he still owes me the very substance of those dirham or what is currently in circulation today. He (the Imam) wrote to me, ‘You have the right to be paid what is current in circulation today as you had given him what was current in circulation among people in those days.’”
